ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6516, as last amended by Act No. 19099); Act on Regulation and Punishment of Concealment of Criminal Proceeds (Act No. 6517, as last amended by Act No. 19098); Commercial Act, Act No. 1000, as last amended by Act No. 19032, including the beneficial ownership disclosure articles applicable to financial institutions and corporations; Financial Services Commission regulations on customer identification under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act; Act on Prohibition of Financing of Terrorism and Financing of Weapons of Mass Destruction, as amended; United Nations Security Council resolutions transposed into Korean law through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs public announcements.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of each corporate ultimate beneficial owner at or above the 25-percent threshold
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate Registry, Companies House, or equivalent competent registry in the country of origin of the ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the issuing country is a member of the Hague Apostille Convention, the certificate must be apostilled by that country's designated central authority and then presented to the Korean registrar with a lawfully certified Korean translation; consular legalization must not be added. If the issuing country is not an Apostille Convention member, the sole valid path is consular legalization at the Korean Embassy or Consulate, never after or in addition to an apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Subsistence for each corporate ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State or national company registry of the ultimate beneficial owner's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path for Hague Apostille Convention members; consular legalization path for non-members; the two authentication systems are parallel and mutually exclusive, and sequential chaining of apostille and consular legalization is prohibited.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing the formation of the Korean Yuhan Hoesa, approving the AML/CFT compliance program, and appointing directors and authorized signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the beneficial owner, with signature of the company secretary notarized by a qualified notary public in the beneficial owner's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization must be followed exclusively by either a Hague apostille from the competent authority or, for non-member states, consular legalization by the Korean diplomatic mission; do not apply both procedures to the same instrument.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association or Memorandum and Articles of Association of each corporate ultimate beneficial owner (signed copy with all amendments)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or statutory corporate records custodian in the ultimate beneficial owner's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille Convention member states, affix apostille only; for non-member states, conduct consular legalization only; the two routes must never be combined sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the ultimate beneficial owner and proposed Korean entity, including account opening history, expected transaction volume, and source-of-wealth attestation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Qualified commercial bank in the ultimate beneficial owner's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank officer's signature must be notarized and then covered solely by an apostille if the bank is located in an Apostille Convention member state or solely by Korean consular legalization if the bank is located in a non-member state; no mixed or sequential authentication is permitted.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All shareholders, directors, officers, ultimate beneficial owners, authorized signatories, and material counterparties must be screened against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit watch-lists, the FATF High-Risk Jurisdictions list, and the domestic sanctions list of the Republic of Korea. Politically Exposed Persons include foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs, international organization PEPs, and their family members and close associates. Enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth documentation, complete beneficial ownership chain tracing to the 25% threshold, senior management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring are mandatory before any equity contribution or lending platform activation. A name or transaction match triggers an immediate Suspicious Transaction Report to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit within 24 hours and a hold on all activities pending competent authority authorization.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office (iROS) of the Supreme Court of Korea (www.iros.go.kr), commercial name clearance module administered by the District Court Registration Office with jurisdiction over the proposed registered office.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Korean Commercial Act, the legal name of a Yuhan Hoesa must be registered in the Korean script; a parallel English or romanized name may appear in the articles only as a secondary trade name and has no independent legal force. The four-tier naming review is: first, distinctiveness from existing registered names in the same registry; second, absence of prohibited or sensitive tokens; third, no false indication of a business type or regulatory status; and fourth, conformity with the licensed business purpose clauses required for a P2P micro-lending platform.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must obtain the written grounds from the iROS registration clerk and may immediately resubmit a corrected name. If the applicant believes the rejection is erroneous, a formal objection must be filed with the head of the competent District Court Registration Office within 14 days from the date of the rejection notice, accompanied by a comparative name table, evidence of the requested business purpose, and a legal memorandum. If the registry upholds the rejection, the applicant may initiate an administrative lawsuit pursuant to the Administrative Litigation Act within 90 days of the final rejection decision. Because the proposed name is suspended during the appeal, the applicant should simultaneously request interim preservation of the name to prevent a competing applicant from taking it.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office, commercial mailbox, or shared desk without a dedicated physical space is not permissible for a licensed P2P micro-lending platform in South Korea. The Korean Commercial Act, the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information, and the Financial Services Commission/FSS interpretative practice require the registered office to be a real, staffed physical location in Korea where statutory books, AML/CFT records, loan files, board meeting minutes, and tax documents are kept and where regulators, tax officers, and external auditors can conduct inspections. Municipal tax offices and Korean commercial banks will reject a mailing-address-only registered office for this industry. A supplementary virtual address may be used for ancillary correspondence only if the physical registered office remains fully compliant.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced inspection: (1) Korean-language signage at the registered address; (2) lease or title documents in the company name; (3) full-time officer or employee presence; (4) statutory registers and AML/CDD files stored on-site; (5) physical or cloud-based server infrastructure with local access evidence; and (6) tax invoices, corporate bank statements, and electronic loan records available at the office. Quantified risk: for a high-risk licensed financial platform, approximately 85% probability of an unannounced inspection by the Financial Supervisory Service or municipal tax authority within the first 12 months of incorporation, and approximately 70% probability of a second inspection within years two and three; the District Court registration examiner typically performs a physical verification visit before final approval of a regulated entity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Korean Commercial Act, Chapter V, Articles 287-2 to 287-45 (Yuhan Hoesa / limited liability company), Article 169; Registration of Commercial Matters Act; Foreign Investment Promotion Act Article 5 for non-resident investors.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Local District Court Registry Office of the jurisdiction where the registered office is located, administered by the Supreme Court of Korea; e-filing through IROS (Internet Registration Office).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa), with notarized Articles of Incorporation, filed with the competent Court Registry Office.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the Korean Commercial Act for a Yuhan Hoesa; the quota capital fixed in the Articles must be fully subscribed and paid before registration. Funds must be deposited in a domestic bank account opened for the company, and the bank's deposit certificate must be annexed to the registration application. There is no blocked escrow account requirement, but invested amounts may not be withdrawn before registration. If the company seeks the Online Investment-Linked Finance Business license, it must additionally satisfy the minimum own-capital requirement prescribed by the Financial Services Commission.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF MANAGERS OF YUHAN HOESA. At a meeting of the founding members and the designated first managers of Yuhan Hoesa (the 'Company'), duly called and held at the Company's proposed registered office in Seoul, Republic of Korea, on the ____ day of ________, 20____, the following resolutions were proposed, seconded, and adopted unanimously by all persons entitled to vote, acting in lieu of a formal meeting in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation and the Korean Commercial Act. WHEREAS the Company is to be organized as a Yuhan Hoesa, a limited liability company, with its registered office in the Republic of Korea and its principal object the operation of an automated algorithmic underwriting platform for micro consumer loans and online investment-linked finance; and WHEREAS the founding members have agreed to subscribe for the entire quota capital of the Company in the amount of KRW ________, divided into ________ quotas, each with a stated value of KRW ________, to be paid in full in cash to a domestic bank account held in the name of the Company before the registration application is filed. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS. 1. Subscription of Quota Capital. That the subscriptions to quota capital set forth in the Subscription and Consent Schedule are accepted, and the first managers are jointly and severally authorized to receive payment of those subscriptions and to obtain the bank capital deposit certificate required by the Court Registry Office. 2. Registered Office. That the registered office of the Company shall be established at ____________________, Seoul, Republic of Korea, and the first managers are authorized to execute a lease or obtain the written consent of the owner, to verify the exact address, and to file the address in the incorporation registration. 3. Banking Authorization. That the Company shall open a domestic corporate deposit and settlement account with ____________________ Bank, and the Managing Director and the Secretary and Compliance Officer are appointed as signatories, either jointly or severally as the Bank may require, for the purpose of receiving subscription funds, holding operating capital, and effecting all routine disbursements related to formation and licensed lending operations. 4. Statutory Officers. That ________ is appointed as Managing Director, ________ is appointed as Secretary and Compliance Officer, and ________ is appointed as Auditor, each to hold office until the first annual meeting and to exercise the powers specified in the Korean Commercial Act and the Articles of Incorporation. 5. Incorporation and Execution. That the Managing Director and the Secretary are jointly and severally authorized to prepare, sign, notarize, submit, and prosecute the incorporation registration application, to make all statutory declarations, to pay all filing fees, and to take every act necessary to obtain the certificate of incorporation and any special financial license under the Online Investment-Linked Finance Act. All of the foregoing resolutions were adopted unanimously and are effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Verification and Notarized Drafting of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: IROS (Internet Registration Office) of the Supreme Court of Korea; Korean Notary Public appointed under the Notary Public Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search on IROS and the trade-name database of the Supreme Court. Draft the Articles of Incorporation in Korean with a certified English translation if foreign members require, specifying the corporate name, business object, proposed registered office, total quota capital, individual subscription amounts, transfer restrictions, manager appointments, and duration. Every founding member must appear before a Korean notary public, produce valid identity documents, and sign the Articles after the notary confirms legal capacity. The notarized Articles must be executed before filing the registration to the Court Registry Office; any amendment after notarization requires re-execution before a notary.
required_dossiers: IROS trade-name search result
Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Certified English translation (if foreign members require)
Passport or national ID copies of all founding members
Notarization certificate from the Korean notary public
Power of attorney if a representative appears by agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed company name is rejected or challenged, select a revised name and repeat the search. If the notary identifies a defect, amend the Articles and re-execute the notarized instrument. If a foreign member cannot present legalized identity documents, complete apostille or consular legalization and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Contribution Payment and Bank Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Duly licensed commercial bank in the Republic of Korea with foreign exchange capability; KOTRA for Foreign Investment Report where non-resident members subscribe.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, establish a provisional contribution account at a duly licensed commercial bank. Each founding member must transfer funds in KRW or convertible foreign currency to the account in the exact amount appearing in the Articles; the bank will issue a certificate of capital contribution deposit stating the aggregate amount and each payer. A foreign investor must additionally report the inward remittance and obtain a Foreign Investment Report Certificate from the Foreign Exchange Officer or KOTRA. If any contribution is made in kind, an independent appraiser's report and contribution inspection report are required; however, cash contributions are recommended for a fintech charter. No withdrawal for formation expenses may be made before registration.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Provisional bank account application form
Proof of remittance or deposit from each founding member
Bank capital deposit certificate
Foreign Investment Report Certificate (for non-resident subscribers)
In-kind contribution appraisal report (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines to issue the deposit certificate because of incomplete anti-money-laundering verification, resubmit ownership and source-of-funds documentation. If the foreign exchange report is rejected, correct the bank code or remittance purpose and re-file before the Court Registry submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Court Registry Office of the registered office jurisdiction; e-filing through IROS.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation registration application electronically through IROS or with the competent Local District Court Registry Office. The application must be in the prescribed statutory form and accompanied by the notarized Articles, deposit certificate, consent forms, and registered office evidence. The registry examines the contents for legal validity. If a prescribed document is missing, the officer will issue a correction order; remedy by submitting corrected forms within the stated grace period. Upon approval, the registry issues the Certificate of Registered Matters and enters the company in the Commercial Registry. Adverse registry rejection may be challenged by immediate appeal to the High Court within two weeks under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act.
required_dossiers: Completed registration application form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank capital deposit certificate
Consent letter of each founding member
Lease agreement or written use permission for the registered office
Corporate seal form and power of attorney (if filed by an agent)
Foreign Investment Report Certificate (if applicable)
Court fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction order, cure all defects within the specified period, generally two weeks, by filing corrected documents. If the application is refused, file an immediate appeal to the High Court under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act within two weeks of the refusal decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax Registration and Online Investment-Linked Finance License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (local branch); Financial Services Commission and Financial Supervisory Service for the specialized P2P lending license.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Court Registry Office confirms incorporation and issues the corporate seal certificate, apply to the local National Tax Service branch for business registration and a corporate tax identification number. Then apply to the Financial Services Commission for Online Investment-Linked Finance Business registration by submitting the operational manual, AML/CTF compliance policy, data security plan, consumer complaint procedure, and credit evaluation methodology. The FSC examines the corporate governance, capital soundness, investor protection measures, and information technology infrastructure. Do not begin accepting investments or disbursing consumer loans until the registration certificate is issued. Upon approval, complete the remaining electronic financial infrastructure approvals and bank API integrations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registered Matters from the Court Registry Office
Corporate seal certificate
Business registration application form (National Tax Service)
Lease agreement and workplace floor plan
FSC Online Investment-Linked Finance Business registration form
AML/CFT policy and information security plan
Consumer protection and credit evaluation manual
Financial statements or capital verification document
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service or FSC returns a query, supplement the requested documents through the respective portal within the objection period. If FSC registration is denied, submit a revised AML and consumer protection plan and request reconsideration, or pursue an administrative appeal through the FSC administrative appeals process.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Services Commission (FSC) and Financial Supervisory Service (FSS); National Tax Service for business registration; Personal Information Protection Commission for data privacy; local municipal government for ordinary business premises.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Online Investment-Linked Finance Business Registration (P2P lending platform) under the Online Investment-Linked Finance Act; where the company extends loans using its own capital, it must also file a Credit Business Registration under the Credit Business Act and maintain the applicable capital, AML, and consumer-protection conditions.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea (Not Applicable)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - Exempt. The registered business is a digital fintech and does not construct, manufacture, assemble, store, or discharge regulated substances. If the company ever owns a physical data center, the owner or operator must separately assess ICT complex or building construction under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no process wastewater, air emissions, or hazardous waste are generated by algorithmic loan underwriting. Standard office waste must be disposed through licensed municipal collectors; discarded electronic equipment must be recycled through licensed e-waste recycling facilities under the Wastes Control Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no civil defense permit for pure office-based fintech. The landlord must maintain fire alarms, extinguishers, emergency lighting, and evacuation routes inspected under the Act on Fire Prevention and Installation, Maintenance, and Safety Control of Fire-Fighting Systems. If the business employs more than the statutory threshold, an occupational workplace safety certificate under the Occupational Safety and Health Act is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr); export customs clearance and export declaration filing administered by Korea Customs Service via UNI-PASS
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity forming a Korean Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) must first complete the required Financial Services Commission registration/licence for P2P micro-lending. The entity must then file a Foreign Corporation Domestic Place of Business Registration application with the competent NTS district tax office, either in person or through the HomeTax portal, submitting certified English and Korean copies of the foreign certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, memorandum and articles, board resolution appointing the Korean tax representative, power of attorney, proof of the Korean domestic place of business (lease agreement or service-office contract), and the foreign entity's own foreign tax identification number. Upon review, NTS issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number (sintae no), which serves simultaneously as the Korean corporate TIN and VAT registration number. If the foreign entity supplies only electronic or digital services and has no Korean fixed place of business, it may instead use the simplified registration procedure for foreign electronic service suppliers, appoint a Korean tax representative, and register through HomeTax before making taxable supplies. The assigned registration number must be used for corporate tax withholding, VAT declarations, e-tax invoice issuance, and Korean Customs Service export filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - A Yuhan Hoesa formed under Korean law is classified as a domestic corporation under the Corporate Tax Act and is taxed at entity level on worldwide income; no pass-through treatment is available to foreign members. If the investor instead operates as a branch of a foreign corporation without a Korean entity, Korean branch taxation applies with territorial sourcing rules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korea does not provide a check-the-box election or hybrid mismatch election. A Korean Yuhan Hoesa is mandatorily entity-level taxable as a domestic corporation under the Corporate Tax Act; foreign members cannot elect pass-through treatment. Only standard corporate governance elections (financial year, tax representative appointment, and foreign tax credit claiming) apply; no tax classification election is permitted.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax) under the Value Added Tax Act; interest from P2P lending is VAT-exempt financial service income, while platform fees and separate service charges are taxable supplies at the standard VAT rate.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 0 for corporations - VAT registration is mandatory from the commencement of any taxable business in Korea. A reduced simplified taxpayer status exists for small individual entrepreneurs with annual taxable supplies not exceeding KRW 80,000,000, but a Yuhan Hoesa corporation is not eligible for that simplification and must register regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All Korean VAT-registered suppliers must issue tax invoices; e-tax invoices are mandatory for substantially all B2B sales and must be digitally signed using an NTS-approved certificate and transmitted to NTS through the HomeTax interoperability API by the day after supply. The NTS assigns and validates each e-tax invoice number in near real-time for anti-fraud integrity. Korean businesses must also participate in the mandatory cash-receipt system for B2C payments where required. For exports, the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS system performs export declaration clearance and data sharing with NTS, creating the fiscal evidence chain for zero-rated export claims.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Statutory zero-rating applies to goods actually exported from Korea when the export declaration is accepted by Korea Customs Service, the exporter is the Korean seller, and the goods physically leave Korea within the statutory period. Services supplied by a Korean resident to a non-resident are zero-rated when performed wholly outside Korea, foreign consideration is paid in foreign currency, and no Korean consumer/property/benefit is involved; qualifying digital electronic services exported to foreign customers may similarly be zero-rated if the foreign recipient and overseas use are evidenced. P2P platform services rendered to foreign lenders/borrowers offshore can qualify for zero-rating if the contractual and actual performance place is outside Korea, while pure lending interest provided to, or consumed by, Korean persons remains VAT-exempt rather than zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration via UNI-PASS (export clearance/shipment confirmation)
Bill of Lading (maritime) or Air Waybill (air) evidencing physical departure of goods from Korean territory
Foreign exchange payment confirmation / Inward remittance certificate issued by a Korean licensed foreign exchange bank showing receipt of export proceeds from the non-resident buyer
Commercial invoice, loan contract, or platform services agreement matching the Korean exporter, foreign counterparty, consideration amount, and invoiced currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS and Korea Customs Service cross-match export declarations, e-tax invoices, customs clearance records, and foreign exchange bank receipts. If export proceeds are not repatriated within 180 days or the customs/fx documentation is incomplete, the zero-rating is disallowed and the supply is reassessed at 10% VAT with late-payment interest penalties. Fraudulent or unverified export zero-rating claims trigger penalty taxes up to 40% of the unpaid tax under the Framework Act on National Taxes, retrospective clawbacks for up to five tax years, customs and foreign exchange regulatory fines, and under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, imprisonment or criminal fines for the entity's directors and responsible tax representative.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), acting as the central bank and foreign exchange reporting authority, in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Financial Services Commission (FSC) for P2P platform licensing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a largely liberalized convertible-currency regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree. The won is fully convertible for bona fide current-account transactions including trade settlements, service receipts, and ordinary dividend remittances, subject to transaction evidence and reporting thresholds. Capital-account transactions, including inbound equity investments, acquisition of domestic financial instruments, and loans, are not freely convertible without filing; residents and non-residents must submit advance or post-transaction FX reports through the Bank of Korea's Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS). For a P2P micro-lending platform, the regulator's authorization under the Online Investment-Linked Financing Act (P2P Act) is a precondition for any cross-border funding conversion. Profit remittance is permissible after audited financials, corporate tax clearance, and formal dividend resolution; however, the borrowing entity must demonstrate that incoming foreign capital was properly registered and used for licensed lending activities. Although current transfer evidence is normally sufficient, the lending platform's 'high-risk financial' classification will trigger beneficial-ownership and source-of-funds scrutiny at the FX bank before conversion.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree, export proceeds must be collected and deposited in a foreign exchange bank within the export collection period of six months from the shipment date unless a bank-approved extension is obtained. No statutory mandatory conversion percentage exists; exporters may retain 100% of foreign currency proceeds in a designated foreign currency account, but any conversion into KRW must be executed through a licensed foreign exchange bank and reported through FEIS. If the six-month deadline is missed without an approved extension, the unrepatriated export receipts become a regulatory violation subject to BOK and MOEF enforcement. For the P2P platform, interest, fees, and commissions received from overseas borrowers or service users are treated as current-account service revenue and must also be received through the licensed FX bank with supporting contracts.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Payoneer, Currenxie, and similar platforms are not licensed foreign exchange banks under the Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. They cannot lawfully open domestic won accounts, access the BOK-Wire+ or KFTC clearing systems, comply with Korea's real-name financial transaction requirements, or service a licensed Korean P2P lending entity's treasury. They should be used only as ancillary downstream payout rails after KRW has been lawfully converted and remitted through a domestic Tier 1 bank. The primary clearing relationship must reside with a Korean commercial bank; reliance on an EMI without such a domestic bank would be a regulatory red flag and is not recommended.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical, in-branch compliance interview is effectively mandatory for a high-risk P2P fintech entity. Korean real-name financial transaction rules require identity verification at account opening, and most Tier 1 banks will require at least one statutory director or a locally registered representative director to appear in person in Seoul. Remote consular proxy opening is rarely accepted and is normally rejected by bank compliance committees for high-risk financial-sector clients. The practical blueprint is for one principal/statutory director to travel to Korea, appear before the bank's FM and AML committee with original corporate documents, and present the business model; alternatively, an appointed in-country representative director with a Korean Alien Registration Card may satisfy the interview if supported by apostilled power of attorney, notarized board resolutions, and a clear beneficial-ownership chart.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear beneficial ownership through a multi-tier non-resident holding structure or nominee director arrangement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registry extract from the Korean court registrar; apostilled certificate of good standing; share register and full beneficial-ownership chain for each shareholder holding over 25%; passport copies and residency proof of all UBOs; a notarized declaration of source of wealth including audited financial statements, investment agreements, and tax records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of demonstrable regulatory authorization to conduct P2P micro-lending in South Korea.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FSC registration certificate under the Online Investment-Linked Financing Act; FSC approval or license for consumer lending; proof of paid-in capital and statutory operational fund segregation; regulatory audit reports; external legal opinion confirming the entity may accept cross-border investment; internal AML/CFT program and transaction monitoring documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicious or unexplained source of foreign capital injection into the Korean treasury account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed cross-border investment agreement and loan agreement; board resolutions of both sending and receiving entities; a reference or SWIFT cover note from the remitting bank; certified source-of-funds statements from the investor; audited corporate accounts and personal tax returns for natural-person investors; a clear narrative of capital flow from source to Korean escrow account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High daily-volume micro-loan disbursements and third-party wallet payouts create layering and commingling risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed treasury flow chart separating investor capital, borrower principal, interest revenue, fees, and escrowed repayments; daily transaction reconciliation reports; an independent AML audit report for the platform; evidence of a designated capital escrow account for cross-border funding; a legal opinion on Korean consumer credit law and borrower disbursement rails.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital for the Korean Yuhan Hoesa must be routed through a licensed foreign exchange bank. For foreign direct investment, file a foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act through the bank or Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) before remittance; for non-equity funding, file the required capital-transaction report under FETA through FEIS. The wire must be sent by SWIFT MT103 to the beneficiary's capital escrow account with the Korean bank, and the purpose code must be selected as 'capital account / equity investment (FDI)' or 'capital account / shareholder loan', not a trade or current-account code. Upon arrival, the bank verifies the source of funds and issues the invested-capital registration or foreign exchange certificate. Capital verification for the corporate registry is based on the bank certificate, board resolution, and receipt of funds into the escrow account; each tranche must match the filed investment report within the declared amount and timeline.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For the P2P lending business, the main outbound rails are local ACH direct debit and wallet payouts through the Korean KFTC and BOK-Wire+ settlement systems, not commercial letters of credit. Cross-border outbound remittances, including foreign shareholder loans, dividends, fees, or trade services, must use SWIFT MT103 through the licensed domestic bank with a matching FETA purpose code and supporting contract. Commercial LC and documentary collections are reserved for genuine goods-trade settlements and should not be used for lending or platform treasury movements. All outbound disbursements must be covered by a board-approved transaction schedule, beneficial payee information, and daily reconciliation. Interest and principal flows must be segregated from platform fee income to avoid regulatory 'collection account' commingling issues.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore forward foreign exchange contracts with a licensed Korean FX bank, permitted only for documented underlying current or capital exposures and reflected in FEIS reporting.
Foreign exchange swaps (FX swaps) for funding-cycle hedging of shareholder loans or foreign debt instruments, subject to FETA transaction classification and underlying contract evidence.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for non-resident investors to hedge KRW exposure, provided they are executed with a licensed FX bank or through an authorized international dealer and settle in USD without illegal onshore KRW conversion.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for approved cross-border borrowings, where the maturity, notional, and coupon match the underlying P2P funding facility; speculative transactions are prohibited.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements Adoption and Ordinary Members' Meeting Approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate record retained at the registered office; financial statements submitted with the corporate income tax return to the National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa, approval of the financial statements must occur by March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No automatic administrative strike-off exists in South Korea; failure to hold the ordinary meeting or to keep financial statements is a Commercial Act violation subject to court-imposed non-compliance fines against directors. If the tax return is also late, NTS levies a 20% non-filing penalty (up to 40% for fraudulent omission) plus 0.022% daily late-payment interest, and the court may order dissolution of the company upon repeated material violation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return with Tax-Based Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via the HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 following a calendar-year fiscal year; within three months after the fiscal year-end if a non-calendar business year is adopted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a 20% penalty on the unpaid tax (40% in cases of fraudulent omission) and 0.022% daily delinquency interest; the tax representative may be placed on the NTS delinquent taxpayer list, assets may be seized, and travel restrictions may be imposed. There is no administrative strike-off under Korean law, but sustained non-compliance can support court-ordered dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent Certified External Auditor's Annual Audit Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the DART electronic disclosure and filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two weeks after the ordinary members' meeting approving the financial statements, and no later than April 14 for a calendar-year entity where the meeting is held by March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit or include a misleading audit report leads to regulatory fines, criminal sanctions against directors and the responsible auditor, and an FSS order to correct or re-audit; deliberate omission may result in the suspension or cancellation of the auditor's registration and suspension of the P2P lending license for regulatory unreliability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business Report of the Online Investment-Linked Finance (P2P Micro-Lending) Platform Operator
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Services Commission (FSC) through the Financial Supervisory Service licensing and supervision division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal year-end; March 31 for calendar-year licensees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or materially false filing supports administrative sanctions including corrective orders, written cautions, business suspension, and revocation of the P2P lending license; the company and its responsible officers may also be criminally prosecuted under the Online Investment-Linked Finance Act and reported to the Korean Supreme Prosecutors' Office.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual AML/CTF Compliance Report and Beneficial Ownership Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) under the Financial Services Commission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 of the year following the reporting calendar year, with suspicious transaction reports and large cash transaction reports filed through the continuous reporting system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omission of the annual AML report, failure to escalate suspicious transactions, or inaccurate beneficial owner confirmation can trigger monetary administrative penalties, criminal liability for officers, heightened corrective supervision, and revocation of the high-risk special license for the micro-lending platform.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Register Audit and Maintenance Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial registry chamber of the local district court on demand; also available for inspection by NTS and FSS examiners during supervision
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous obligation, with a full year-end verification by December 31; any change in members, directors, or registered charges must be recorded in the relevant statutory register within two weeks of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain the registered office registers makes ownership transfers ineffective against the company, exposes directors to administrative fines, undermines audit assurance, and can be used by creditors or the court as evidence of management defect supporting judicial dissolution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Yuhan Hoesa is compulsorily subject to an independent certified CPA audit under the Korean External Audit Act if its total assets at fiscal year-end equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.1 million). No separate statutory turnover or headcount threshold is imposed by Korean law. However, a licensed online investment-linked finance P2P micro-lending platform is required to undergo an external audit regardless of asset size under the Online Investment-Linked Finance Act and FSC licensing conditions. In addition, any company that is publicly listed, conducts a public offering, or belongs to a consolidated external-audit group is mandatorily audited.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards, substantively aligned with IASB IFRS) is required for mandatory statutory audits and is the framework directed by the FSC for licensed financial and P2P lending platforms. P2P loan receivables must be measured applying K-IFRS 9 expected credit loss methodology. Non-audited private entities may apply Korean GAAP or K-SME accounting standards, but the licensed micro-lending platform in this payload falls under FSC audit supervision and therefore must use K-IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Korean Commercial Act, the Yuhan Hoesa must keep an accurate register of members at its registered office and record any transfer, pledge, or change in ownership interests promptly, with a maximum two-week recording window for register updates after the event. South Korea does not maintain a public annual UBO form for ordinary LLCs, but the licensed P2P platform must satisfy FSC and KoFIU AML due-diligence rules by confirming the beneficial owners of the legal entity and its financing partners at least annually; whenever there is a change in shareholding or beneficial ownership control requiring regulatory acknowledgement, the updated beneficial ownership declaration must be submitted to the FSC within 30 days of the execution of the transfer. Failure to update the member register means the transfer cannot be asserted against the company, and the transferor remains liable for unpaid statutory contributions.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 - USD 1,200 per year for a commercial registered-office address and registered-office agent or local corporate secretarial support in Seoul or Busan
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 30,000 per year for a licensed micro-lending platform requiring a K-IFRS external audit, DART filing, and FSC reporting support

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax rate on taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion (progressive: 9% up to KRW 200 million; 19% from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 21% from KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion; 24% above KRW 300 billion), plus a 10% local income tax surcharge on the national corporate tax payable, resulting in a combined top effective statutory rate of 26.4%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No blanket tax holiday for fintech/P2P platforms, but a Korea-resident LLC may avail itself of: (1) R&D tax credit up to 25% of qualifying R&D expenditure on credit-scoring algorithm development and underwriting software under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act (STTCL); (2) SME venture business corporate tax rate reductions and up to 50% income tax exemption for qualifying venture enterprises; (3) Free Economic Zone (FEZ) regional headquarters incentives (50% corporate tax reduction for 5 years and 20% for the next 2 years); (4) no patent box regime, so licensing income from IP is taxed at ordinary rates; interest/dividend income from foreign sources may be eligible for foreign tax credits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean Corporate Income Tax Return (Corporate Tax Act Form 1: Corporation Tax Base and Tax Return / Self-Assessment Return) filed through the National Tax Service (NTS) HomeTax electronic filing portal; non-resident branches use the same form with additional branch-accounting schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (business year), with two mandatory semi-annual prepayment submissions for most corporations (interim prepayment due July 31 for a December fiscal year-end), plus an additional estimated-payment regime for large corporations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year entity, the filing deadline is March 31 of the following year. Foreign-owned and multinational entities with foreign offices or foreign transactions may obtain an automatic 1-month extension to April 30 by filing an extension notice. Any further extension must be approved by the NTS and generally cannot extend beyond July 31 of the filing year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the legal entity name (Yuhan Hoesa), business registration number (business use ID), head office address, representative director name, industry code (ISIC 6499 / NAICS 522299), and the designated tax office.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean LLC is a domestic corporation if its head office or place of effective management is in Korea; therefore, it must report worldwide income. Non-resident ownership does not change the entity's Korean tax residency. Include the valid FSC online lending platform registration number in the remarks column; failure to maintain a valid financial license will be reported to relevant regulators and may invalidate certain expense deductions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State the first and last dates of the fiscal year reported; normally 12 months.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a non-resident parent requires a different fiscal year, the Korean entity may apply for NTS permission to adopt a special fiscal year. Any change of fiscal year must be filed before the end of the first reporting cycle, and NTS may deny the change if it is deemed to distort taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report total operating revenues: loan interest income earned by the platform's own loan portfolio, platform arrangement fees, servicing fees, late-payment fees, commitment fees, and other recurring lending-related income derived by the Korean fintech entity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the accrual basis under Korean GAAP or K-IFRS. Funds collected from retail lenders and immediately passed through to borrowers are not platform revenue; only the platform's own net interest margin, fee spread, and commissions are reportable. For loans originated through automated underwriting algorithms, recognize interest as earned, and cannot defer income by keeping an internal 'reserve' unless expressly permitted by Korean tax law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Cost of Sales / Direct Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter direct costs: funding interest paid to lenders/investors where the platform borrows from them, loan origination system amortization, direct customer acquisition costs, data and hosting charges, credit bureau charges, and loan loss provisions directly tied to revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to foreign related-party lenders is deductible only if arm's length and within the thin-capitalization safe harbor (debt-equity ratio 3:1 for loans from a foreign major shareholder; otherwise interest disallowance under LCITA Article 14). For non-resident lenders receiving Korean-source interest, the Korean borrower/platform may be required to withhold 22% (20% tax plus 2% local surcharge) unless the lender files a treaty-rate application. Substantiate all cross-border service and funding arrangements with written agreements, transfer pricing studies, and bank records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed as Gross Revenue (Box 3) less Cost of Sales (Box 4); for a P2P lending entity this represents the net lending margin plus fee income before operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: NTS reviews gross margin against comparables; if the Korean platform reports a chronic gross margin below the arm's-length range, it may be required to file a transfer pricing adjustment. Record gross margin in the statutory TP Local File to substantiate the functional profile.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Selling, General, and Administrative Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Salaries and wages, office rent, utilities, IT security, regulatory compliance costs, financial statement audit fees, legal fees, advertising, bad-debt expenses (loan-loss allowances and write-offs), and other SG&A.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be supported by Korean invoices, employment contracts, and evidence of actual payment in Korea. Non-deductible expenses (entertainment in excess of statutory limits, certain donations, fines) must be added back. Management fees paid by the Korean entity to a foreign parent or foreign software affiliate are deductible only with an executed cost-plus or fee agreement and with a TP documentation package; excessive charges may be reclassified as dividends, triggering 22% withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report foreign exchange gains, deposit interest, dividend income from subsidiaries, gains from disposal of securities, and other non-operating income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All Korean-source and foreign-source items reported are taxable as ordinary income unless specifically exempted. Dividend income from a foreign subsidiary qualifies for the dividend-received deduction/participation exemption only if shareholding and business substance requirements are met. Do not omit income from overseas bank accounts; a failure to report may also trigger the Korean CFC regime and anti-avoidance consequences.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report losses on disposal of assets, impairment losses, donations, penalties, and other non-operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tax fines, overdue tax surcharges, and all forms of punitive penalties are not deductible. Impairment of receivables in a fintech loan portfolio must be evidenced by objective default data and the NTS loan-loss criteria; any write-off of intercompany debt should be supported by an arm's-length credit analysis. Payments to non-resident parties for consulting, insurance, or settlement may be subject to 22% withholding if they constitute Korean-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Book income equal to Gross Profit (Box 5) + Non-Operating Income (Box 7) - Non-Operating Expenses (Box 8), before tax-reconciliation adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This box will be reconciled in the tax-adjustment schedule. Ensure that the accounting profit is aligned with the audited Korean financial statements; if the company is exempt from statutory audit, retain internal financial statements that reconcile to the tax return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 - Taxable Income Adjustments and Loss Carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The tax return reconciliation section: add back non-deductible book expenses, subtract non-taxable book income, include transfer pricing adjustments, apply interest disallowances (thin cap), and deduct available tax-loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach all required schedules: loss carryforward schedule, tax-exempt income, entertainment expense disallowance, and the TP adjustment schedule. A Korean domestic corporation can carry forward net operating losses for 10 years (15 years for SMEs); however, a change of/or substantial alteration in equity may restrict loss carryforward under the continuity-of-ownership rule. If a non-resident parent owns more than 50% and the entity has median operations, substantiate the arm's-length financing and pricing in this reconciliation to avoid a 40% penalty later.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The final positive taxable income amount after all adjustments, deductions, and carryforwards, to be applied to the progressive corporate income tax schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Round the tax base to the nearest KRW won and compute the national corporate income tax at the four-tier progressive rates. If the entity has a nil tax base, still file by the statutory deadline with complete schedules to preserve carryforwards and avoid the non-filing penalty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 12 - National Corporate Income Tax Computed
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The amount of national corporate income tax derived by applying the statutory progressive rate schedule to the tax base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not deduct the local income tax surcharge here; local surcharge is reported separately in Box 14. If there are foreign source income credits, apply them after the national tax is computed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report and apply foreign income tax credits, R&D tax credits, employment tax credits, and other STTCL incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are limited to the Korean tax attributable to the foreign-source income; attach foreign tax payment certificates and income source breakdowns. R&D credits for algorithm underwriting require technical documentation describing the R&D project, personnel, and finality. Excess credits may carry forward up to 5 years depending on the provision; otherwise they are lost.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The local income tax (local surtax) on corporate income, computed at 10% of the national corporate income tax computed in Box 12 after non-refundable credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Even if national tax is reduced by credits, the local surcharge is based on the tax payable after certain credits, and it too is subject to international treaty relief? No, local surcharge generally follows national tax and is not automatically relieved under most DTAs; plan for it in profit repatriation projections.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 15 - Prepayments and Interim Tax Payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter all corporate income tax amounts already paid during the year: interim prepayments, semi-annual payments, and any estimated taxes paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile with the NTS claim for payment; overpayment becomes a refund or credit against the following year. For non-resident-owned Korean entities, interim prepayments based on prior-year tax may significantly exceed actual liability in a loss year; file the optional adjusted-interim tax return to reduce the prepayment if prior-year taxable income has dropped.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax payable = Box 12 - Box 13 + Box 14 - Box 15. If negative, the amount is refundable subject to NTS audit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Arrange payment by the statutory deadline via electronic transfer or bank payment. Payment delays trigger daily late-payment interest of 0.022%. The NTS may offset refunds against other outstanding national tax, and refunds to foreign parent companies are generally paid only after clearance of the non-resident shareholder's withholding obligations on subsequent dividends.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing causes a non-declaration surcharge of 20% of the unpaid tax if filed within one month after the deadline, and 40% if filed later or where the understatement is fraudulent; underreporting surcharges are 10% for negligent understatement and 40% for unlawful/fraudulent understatement; late payment incurs a daily 0.022% surcharge. Intentional tax evasion creates exposure under the Act on the Punishment of Tax Evaders to imprisonment of up to five years and fines of up to three times the tax evaded, along with administrative blacklisting and possible immigration/cross-border travel restrictions for responsible directors.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Statutory outbound dividend withholding tax is 20% under the Corporate Income Tax Act / Income Tax Act, plus a 2% local income tax surcharge (10% on the withholding tax), producing an aggregate 22% withholding on dividends paid by the Korean LLC to non-resident shareholders, unless reduced under a bilateral Double Tax Treaty (DTA). Some DTAs reduce the withholding rate to 10% or 15%; parent-subsidiary-type reductions may be available for qualifying shareholdings.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced treaty dividend, interest, or royalty rate, the payor (or the beneficial owner) must submit to the NTS the 'Application for Exemption from or Reduction of Korean Tax pursuant to a Tax Treaty' (Form No. 21) together with: (1) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the home jurisdiction of the non-resident recipient, apostilled or consularized as required; (2) a beneficial-ownership statement and supporting substance evidence (board minutes, office lease, employees, decision-making records, financial statements); (3) the underlying contract (loan agreement, license agreement, or shareholder resolution declaring the dividend); and (4) a completed withholding-rate reconciliation. The NTS may issue a clearance certificate authorizing the lower rate before payment, typically within 2-6 weeks. If clearance is not obtained before payment, the payer must withhold at the 22% statutory rate; the non-resident recipient may then file a treaty refund claim within 5 years, subject to a full substance review. The Korean LLC is the withholding agent for dividends paid on its shares and must remit the tax to the NTS within 10 days of the end of the month in which the dividend is paid.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory 20% plus 2% local surcharge (22% total); under DTAs, interest rates are commonly reduced to 10% (or 0% for qualifying public entities) where the beneficial owner is the lender; arm's-length financing documentation and TRC are required. Royalties (intellectual property, software, algorithms): statutory 20% plus 2% local surcharge (22% total); DTA rates range from 10% to 15% (e.g., US 15%, Germany 15%, Japan 10%, Netherlands 12.5%) with updated beneficial-ownership requirements. For P2P lending, interest accrued to non-resident investors or lenders on Korean resident borrowers is Korean-source income subject to withholding; the platform, as a mandated withholding agent, must remit the tax monthly to the NTS.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Triggering thresholds under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs (LCITA) and its Presidential Decree: Local File is mandatory for a Korean entity when cross-border related-party transactions in each category are at least KRW 5 billion for goods, KRW 2 billion for services, KRW 2 billion for intangibles, and KRW 3 billion for financing/loan transactions; Master File is required when total aggregate intercompany transactions with foreign related parties exceed KRW 100 billion; Country-by-Country Report is required for a multinational group with consolidated revenue above KRW 1 trillion. Even below these thresholds, a taxpayer must retain contemporaneous reasonable-basis documentation if claiming a refund or offset.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not have a standalone 'Economic Substance Regulations' statute, but the general anti-avoidance rule under LCITA Article 4 allows the NTS to recharacterize transactions lacking bona fide economic substance, and the Korean CFC regime under LCITA Article 17 will attribute the passive income of an offshore shell entity to the Korean shareholder unless the offshore entity shows real business substance (actual offices, employees, revenues and management). For a P2P micro-lending platform, the Korean LLC must demonstrate that its core income-generating activities (lending decisions, loan-servicing algorithms, risk management, treasury and compliance) are performed from Korea with local staff and decision-makers; a bare holding or conduit arrangement without such substance will not qualify for treaty relief on outbound payments and may trigger punitive penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Corporate Income Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully omitting loan interest and platform fee income from Box 3, fabricating bad-debt write-offs or loan loss allowances, inflating management fees paid to an offshore affiliate, and using round-trip fund flows or phantom algorithms to shift Korean lending profits to a tax haven entity while presenting false financial statements to the NTS.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Act on the Punishment of Tax Evaders, Article 3: imprisonment for not more than 5 years or a criminal fine of not more than three times the amount of tax evaded, or both; in addition, the NTS will impose the 40% fraud penalty under the Framework Act on National Taxes and daily late-payment surcharge of 0.022%; the unpaid tax will bear interest and enforcement seizures over the corporate assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under the National Tax Collection Act Article 11, a director who actively participated in the evasion becomes secondarily liable for the company's unpaid national taxes if the corporate assets are insufficient; the director's personal bank accounts, real estate and vehicles may be seized. Criminal prosecution can lead to imprisonment up to 5 years; and the NTS may place the director on the tax-delinquent blacklist and impose an overseas travel ban (immigration restriction) until the assessed tax is deposited.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation / Thin Capitalization Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately under-pricing loan defaults, setting unreasonable cross-border interest rates between the Korean P2P platform and a foreign related-party funding vehicle above the arm's-length range, or maintaining a debt-to-equity ratio exceeding 3:1 for loans from a foreign major shareholder so as to inflate interest deductions and strip Korean taxable income; failing to prepare or submit the Master/Local File after exceeding statutory thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: LCITA Article 4 (arm's-length adjustment), Article 14 (thin-capitalization interest disallowance), and Article 16 (transfer pricing documentation penalty). The NTS may recompute the taxable income, disallow excess interest, and impose an additional penalty of up to 20% of adjusted tax and an ad-valorem penalty for non-submission of documents; the statute of limitations for TP adjustments is 5 years (10 in fraud cases).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If a director personally signed false TP documentation or knowingly directed interest payments to a shell entity, the court may classify the action as fraudulent tax evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and impose imprisonment; the director may also be civilly liable to the Korean entity and minority shareholders for the amount of tax, penalties, and interest through a derivative action. NTS may pierce the corporate veil in extreme cases and recover unpaid taxes from the director if the entity's use of the shell company was so integrated that the corporate structure was a sham; a travel ban and asset freeze are typical collection enforcement measures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed P2P Lending / AML and Financial Regulations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an online P2P micro-lending platform in Korea without a valid registration under the Act on Online Investment-Linked Financing Facilities (P2P Lending Act) or the Loan Business Act; commingling client funds, accepting deposits without the necessary banking license, failing to conduct customer due diligence or suspicious transaction reporting, or using the platform as a conduit to launder criminal proceeds on behalf of benefitting ultimate shareholders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Act on Online Investment-Linked Financing Facilities provides criminal penalties of imprisonment for up to 5 years and fines up to KRW 100 million; the Loan Business Act imposes the same criminal range for unlicensed lending; the Financial Services Commission may order immediate shutdown and cancellation of registration. Violations of the Proceeds of Crime Act may result in additional imprisonment of up to 5 years and confiscation of the laundered assets; foreign-exchange registration violations add to the exposure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil will be pierced where the director acted as the 'actual operator' (real controlling person). Directors face personal criminal liability with imprisonment up to 5 years and massive fines; they are also subject to the confiscation of personal property traceable to the illicit proceeds; the FSC may ban them from all financial-industry positions; and customs/immigration authorities can impose a travel ban during investigation and prosecution. If the company is used purely as a shell, the court will treat the company as the director's alter ego and hold the director personally liable for all unpaid civil damages and refunds to defrauded P2P lenders.
